summary:
Whisper stayed locked at faster-whisper-medium through 2026, but the reason the fix "held" changed twice, and that's the actual story. First round I chased a KV-cache budget between two models sharing a GPU — trimmed a context window, freed some memory, verified it, called it done. It broke again two weeks later. Turned out the real cause was upstream of anything I'd touched: one service auto-sizes its GPU allocation at startup and the other loads lazily on first use, so whoever wins the boot-order race gets the card. Three reboots of the identical config gave three different memory splits. The fix wasn't a number, it was pinning the number instead of letting it auto-negotiate.

I built a Japanese-learning app for myself from scratch — lexicon, grammar engine, spaced-repetition drills, speech synthesis and recognition, the works. The interesting failures were less about any one model and more about a system slowly discovering its own scope. A verb-conjugation gap sat unnoticed for months because the content that would have exposed it was buried at position 325 of a 339-word list — nobody ever practiced far enough to hit it. When I finally promoted it earlier, three audio clips turned out to be saying the wrong word entirely, and a health check that looked fine (200 OK) had been silently skipping the check it claimed to run.

On the image side, I run two different generation backends — a local GPU pipeline and a hosted API — and picked between them per job based on what the job actually needed: counting, composition, and negation broke the local model in ways no amount of prompting fixed, so those went to the other one. Style matching went the other way; a newer model version looked better in isolation but rendered with reflections and gradients that didn't match 200+ existing images, so newer lost to "matches."

Underneath most of this is the same recurring bug shape: a guard that used to catch something quietly stops catching it as the data grows around it — a test asserting a coincidence instead of a rule, a rate whose denominator crept past what it was calibrated for. I've started treating "the test is green" and "the test still means anything" as two separate questions.

highlights.oneLiner: GPU auto-sizing raced against Whisper's lazy load; fix was pinning layers, not tuning KV cache
Arbitrating a shared GPU across models exposed a boot-order race no config review would catch
Routing image jobs between local and hosted backends by what each actually handles well
